subject: Television & Streaming
title: Why We Stopped Watching Together
description: A short lesson to help you apply Why We Stopped Watching Together.

hook.text: In 1983, 106 million Americans watched the M*A*S*H finale at the same time. That kind of event is now extinct.

buildup.text: For decades, families gathered around one TV at one time. If you missed it, you waited for summer reruns.

discovery.text: DVRs let people time-shift. Suddenly, nobody had to watch anything live. The shared schedule began to crack.

twist.text: Streaming finished what DVRs started. Now everyone watches different shows at different times on different screens.

climax.text: The watercooler moment—where everyone discussed last night's episode—became rare, then nearly impossible.

punchline.text: We got infinite choice and lost the shared experience.

quiz.question: What technology first allowed viewers to break free from broadcast schedules?
